evidence: Flash and Bambaataa were contemporaries in the same early-to-mid-1970s South Bronx DJ circuit, each developing turntable and sound system techniques independently and in dialogue with the same park-jam audience. This is broad scene history repeated across accounts like Jeff Chang's 'Can't Stop Won't Stop' rather than a single sourced quotation.

earlier.artist: Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five
earlier.title: The Adventures of Grandmaster Flash on the Wheels of Steel

later.title: Planet Rock

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Flash's record is turntable collage: cut breakbeats stitched together live by hand. Bambaataa's, a year later, is the same park-jam instinct rebuilt entirely on synthesizers and a drum machine. Same scene, same era, two different answers to the same problem.

explanation.age7: Flash and Bambaataa were both DJs in the same neighborhood, working out new tricks at the same time.
explanation.age13: Flash and Bambaataa were both DJing park jams and block parties in the South Bronx from the mid-1970s, each inventing techniques, quick-mixing and cutting for Flash, eclectic crate-digging and later synthesizers for Bambaataa, in the same scene at the same time.
explanation.adult: Flash and Bambaataa are best understood as parallel inventors within one scene rather than a strict influence chain in either direction. Crediting a single originator for South Bronx DJ technique oversimplifies a scene where several DJs were developing overlapping ideas concurrently.
